One camera, one ground plane: the camera is about 1.6 metres (5.3 feet) above the ground, so the horizon line of Image 1 passes through both men's chests, and both men stand on that same ground plane, in front of the background objects, not floating above them. Both men are about 1.75 metres (5.7 feet) tall, so every background object keeps its real size relative to them: anything several metres tall (a tree, a lander, a building) stays several times taller than a standing man and must not shrink to fit the frame. Image 2 shows Barnaby, one man in two views, not two people: keep his face, hair, glasses, cardigan and pencil unchanged. Image 3 shows Ambrose, one man in two views, not two people: keep his face, wig, coat and cravat unchanged. Barnaby stands in the left third of the frame and Ambrose stands in the right third, each seen full-length from head to foot with both feet clearly on the ground, the same size, the same distance from the camera, at life-size scale with the location, both turned three-quarters toward each other and toward the camera so both faces stay clearly visible, with clear space above their heads and below their feet. Relight both men to match Image 1's own sunlight exactly — its direction, warm colour temperature and contrast — not the flat, even studio lighting of Image 2/3; their clothing, hair and face keep their own colours, only the lighting on them changes. Each man casts a soft, visible contact shadow on the ground directly beneath his own feet, matching the shadows already in Image 1. A little of the nearest foreground terrain overlaps the lowest part of his legs or feet, so each man reads as standing inside the scene, not cut out and pasted on top of it. At 0.00 seconds Ambrose stares at Barnaby, holding the red apple at chest height in his left hand, and Barnaby lowers his right hand to his side. subject_definitions:
<Picture 1> is the first frame of [Shot 1], showing the Garden of Eden at golden evening: a lush orchard around the Tree of Knowledge, heavy with red apples, a serpent coiled in its branches, and far in the background two small distant figures, a man and a woman modestly covered by leaves and drapery, standing together near the tree, soft low sunlight from behind the camera and slightly to the left, with <Subject 1> and <Subject 2> already standing in place as described below.
<Subject 1> is Barnaby, shown in <Picture 2>, with a wild halo of frizzy white hair, a thick white moustache, a weathered round face, round wire-rimmed glasses, a mustard-yellow cardigan and a pencil behind his right ear.
<Subject 2> is Ambrose, shown in <Picture 3>, with a long wavy grey wig, a long narrow face with deep-set eyes, a long dark brown coat and a white linen cravat.

summary:
A 8-second 16:9 slow push-in wide two-shot that begins from <Picture 1>. <Subject 2> raises one finger and objects. Ends with <Subject 2> with his right forefinger raised, and <Subject 1> with his head tilted.

detailed_description:
Live-action film footage, horizontal 16:9 framing, a science comedy, soft low evening sunlight from behind the camera and slightly to the left, soft gentle contrast, natural skin tones, natural film look.
[Shot 1] The shot begins from <Picture 1>: a horizontal wide two-shot at eye level in the setting of <Picture 1>, keeping its layout and light. At the start of the shot, <Subject 1> stands in the left third of the frame and <Subject 2> stands in the right third, each seen full-length from head to foot with both feet clearly on the ground, the same size, the same distance from the camera, at life-size scale with the setting, both turned three-quarters toward each other and toward the camera so both faces stay clearly visible, with clear space above their heads and below their feet. The camera then slowly and smoothly pushes in throughout the rest of the shot, tightening toward a medium two-shot centered slightly on <Subject 2> by the end, to emphasize his comeback. Far in the background and out of focus, the serpent coils slowly around a low branch of the Tree of Knowledge, and the woman reaches up, picks an apple, and offers it to the man beside her, who takes a slow bite — an unhurried loop of the same small gesture, repeating throughout the shot, too far away for any detail or expression to read, unrelated to and unaffected by what <Subject 1> and <Subject 2> do or say in the foreground. At 0.00 seconds <Subject 2> stares at <Subject 1>, holding the red apple at chest height in his left hand, and <Subject 1> lowers his right hand to his side. At 1.00 seconds <Subject 2> (S2) says it in a low-pitched, crisp, formal, proud voice with a refined English accent, the voice in <Audio 2>: <d>[English] Not a pull? Newton's laws still work for a great many things.</d> Exactly as the voice stops, the lips close and the jaw ceases all speaking motion. This single line is the only speech in the video. <Subject 1> stays silent with closed lips and tilts his head. At 3.00 seconds <Subject 2> raises his right forefinger. At 6.30 seconds <Subject 2> finishes, and both stay silent with closed lips until the final frame. The camera's own slow push-in is the only camera movement in this shot; it does not replace any character action or dialogue below. All motion happens at natural real-time speed, not slow motion. The push-in is smooth, slow and continuous, with no sudden movement or cut, completing by the final frame. At 8.00 seconds, the shot ends on <Subject 2> with his right forefinger raised, and <Subject 1> with his head tilted. There are no subtitles, captions, on-screen text, logos or watermarks anywhere in frame.
